# [TASK] Sanitize hardcoded passwords and default secret disclosures across application configs, Dockerfiles, docs, and Postman collection

## Task
Audit and remove all hardcoded secret fallbacks and password disclosures (including `admin123`, `redis123`, `postgres123`, and JWT secrets) from application configs, Dockerfiles, documentation markdown files, bash scripts, and Postman collection descriptions across the entire repo.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Eliminate hardcoded default password strings from `application.yml` files, `Dockerfile`s, and code comments
- [x] Update Postman collection descriptions and documentation runbooks to use variable placeholders (e.g. `${MONGO_PASSWORD}`)
- [x] Ensure local dev environment (`infrastructure/docker/.env`) supplies required environment variables so local stack execution (`start-infrastructure.sh`, `smoke-test.sh`) remains 100% green
- [x] Verify build and unit/integration tests pass cleanly

## Estimate
**Hours:** 4

## Notes
No `admin123`/`redis123`/`postgres123` remain in any tracked source file, Dockerfile, or the Postman collection. Verified against the live stack with `smoke-test.sh`.

Removing the hardcoded fallbacks broke property binding wherever a test profile never supplied a replacement — fixed in `deb3d67`: api-gateway's `GatewayIntegrationTest` (empty JWT secret, plus a test class that hardcoded the removed default) and movie-service (`REDIS_PORT`/`MONGODB_URI` binding to empty strings, plus a missing `@ActiveProfiles("test")`).

Known follow-up, not blocking: movie-service's `application-test.yml` excludes Redis autoconfiguration by Spring Boot 3.x class names. This project is on Boot 4.1, where that package moved, so the exclusion has been a silent no-op since the upgrade.
